title: Verified mixed-regularity contraction for relaxed Peaceman–Rachford splitting
description:
For actual relaxed PRS iterates and a supplied fixed point in an arbitrary real Hilbert space, the exact C43 distance bound holds when strong convexity and smoothness lie in opposite summands, in either orientation. Also establishes the general auxiliary estimate and mixed decrease and distance bounds.

The new formal work identifies differentiable subgradients, proves an extended-real strong-convexity support inequality, combines strong monotonicity and cocoercivity with the exact proximal energy identity, and checks the three-vector norm bound and square-root factor in both orientations. It also establishes the complete auxiliary-term, mixed-decrease and distance estimates.

Exact hypotheses: Arbitrary complete real inner-product space. Proper closed convex extended-real f,g; actual proximal maps supplied at positive gamma. z(k+1)=(1-lambda(k))*z(k)+lambda(k)*TPRS(z(k));0<lambda(k)<=1; a fixed point zs is supplied. Positive mu,beta. Either f is mu-strongly convex and g has a smooth convex real representative with beta^-1-Lipschitz gradient, or vice versa. sqrt(1-(4*lambda/3)*min(gamma*mu,beta/gamma,1-lambda)) Four nonnegative regularity parameters; smooth representatives required only when the corresponding beta is positive. Full exact signatures in targets/ are authoritative.

Original mathematics: Damek Davis and Wotao Yin, Faster convergence rates of relaxed Peaceman-Rachford and ADMM under regularity assumptions, arXiv:1407.5210v3 (1 May 2015), printed pp. 8 and 16, Theorems 2.1 and 4.3. Exact source bytes were inspected and hashed; the paper is cited, not redistributed.
